claims.claim: Body measurement, pattern measurement and finished garment measurement are three different numbers, and a fitting failure is often a mistranslation between them rather than a sewing error — though non-pattern causes such as construction, pressing, grain and fabric produce the same signs and are ruled out first.
claims.risk_note: If false, the whole diagnostic frame collapses into 'sew better'.

claims.claim: A fit sign is an observation and a cause is an inference; the place a sign appears is not necessarily the place it originates.
claims.risk_note: If false, readers may correctly cut where they see the sign and the book's core method is unnecessary.

claims.claim: The natural waist must be physically marked before any vertical measurement is taken, because vertical measurements are defined from it.
claims.risk_note: Unmarked waist makes vertical measures non-repeatable; every length diagnosis downstream is noise.

claims.claim: The tape must stay parallel to the floor and must not compress the tissue; a tape pulled tight records a smaller body than the one that will wear the garment.
claims.source_support_note: S-0006 BİREBİR: 'the tape sits parallel to the floor and lies snug but does not compress the skin.' İkinci yarısı (sıkı şerit küçük vücut kaydeder) kitabın çıkarımıdır.
claims.risk_note: Systematically undersized measurements produce garments that are too tight everywhere and look like a size problem.

claims.claim: A measurement that is not repeatable is not a measurement. The survey manual behind many published body measurements builds repeat measurement into its quality control, though it does so by having a second, expert examiner repeat the reading rather than by having one person measure twice. Taking each critical measure twice yourself and recording the difference is this book's adaptation of that idea to a reader working alone or with one helper.
claims.risk_note: Kaynağın yordamı İKİ FARKLI ÖLÇÜMCÜ arasındaki farkı ölçer; kitabınki AYNI kişinin kendi tekrarlanabilirliğini ölçer. İkisi aynı şey DEĞİLDİR ve iddia artık bunu söylüyor.

claims.claim: The difference between full bust and high bust is what pattern companies use to decide whether a reader should step down a size and treat the bust separately. It is a size-selection input; it is not a published measure of how much shaping to add. Bra cup sizing uses a different difference again — bust minus underbust — and the two must not be substituted for each other.
claims.risk_note: ÖNCEKİ HÂLİ kap ölçüsünün tanımını 'the clothing-size standard'a atfediyordu. O standart (ISO 8559-1) EDİNİLMEDİ ve maddesi OKUNMADI; okunmamış bir belgenin ne dediği okura söylenemez. İddia, atıf olmadan da doğru olan ayrımla sınırlandı.

claims.claim: Body measurements change over time and should be retaken periodically rather than reused indefinitely.
claims.source_support_note: S-0003 BİREBİR: 'Measurements should be taken at least every 6 months and/or when weight or the figure has varied significantly.'
claims.risk_note: Stale measurements are diagnosed as pattern faults.

claims.claim: Pattern sizing and ready-to-wear sizing are separate systems and the reader's shop size does not predict the pattern size. The guides this book works from assume the distinction rather than state it; they instruct the reader to select from the company's own size chart every time, which is the operative rule either way.
claims.risk_note: Atıfta S-0007 (E-419) vardı; o belge bu turda İLK KEZ okundu ve kalıp/hazır giyim beden ayrımından HİÇ söz etmiyor — uyum bileşenlerini (grain, ease, dart, seam placement) anlatıyor. Atıf KALDIRILDI.

claims.claim: Ease is the difference between the finished garment measurement and the body measurement, and it separates into wearing ease (movement) and design ease (silhouette). Published wearing-ease figures differ between sources and between garment types, so a pattern's own finished measurements are the authority for that pattern.
claims.risk_note: Without the split, readers remove design ease and produce garments that no longer match the design they chose.

claims.claim: A bodice pattern is drafted to one assumed difference between its own high bust and full bust, and companies state different figures. Compare your own difference with the figure the pattern in your hand states: if it is no larger, take the size from the full bust; if it is larger, take the size from the high bust and treat the bust volume as a separate adjustment.
claims.risk_note: Choosing by full bust oversizes the shoulder, neckline and armhole to fix a bust-only shortfall.

claims.claim: Which measurement selects the size for a skirt or trousers is not settled: some pattern companies select by the waist and move to the hip only when the hip is much larger, and others select by the full hip on the grounds that hip adjustments are harder. Follow the instruction printed with the pattern in your hand.
claims.risk_note: Choosing by waist forces the hardest adjustment on the reader unnecessarily.

claims.claim: A flat pattern measurement is only comparable to a body measurement after seam allowances, darts and overlaps have been accounted for.
claims.source_support_note: S-0003 BİREBİR: 'Pin in darts, pleats or gathers as though sewn. Measure from seamline to seamline.' — S-0002: 'Do not include darts or seam allowances in any of the measurements.'
claims.risk_note: Uncorrected flat measurement makes every pattern look too small and triggers unnecessary adjustments.

claims.claim: Toile fabric choice is a real and contested decision rather than a settled rule: match weight, drape and stretch to the fashion fabric when the fault being hunted is drape-dependent, and use a plain stable calico for skeleton fitting of length, width, balance and dart position.
claims.risk_note: A stiff calico toile of a drapey design produces folds that will never appear in the real garment.

claims.claim: Centre front, centre back, the grainlines and horizontal reference lines at bust, waist and hip are marked on the toile before it is worn, because these lines are the reference against which displacement is read; they are read against the room — horizontals parallel to the floor, verticals perpendicular to it.
claims.risk_note: Without reference lines, seam displacement cannot be distinguished from a garment simply sitting askew.

claims.claim: A measurement read from a toile is invalid unless you know where the stitching line is. It is the stitching line, not the seam allowance width, that must match the pattern — standard toile practice cuts wider allowances and marks the seamline so the garment can be let out.
claims.risk_note: A half-inch discrepancy at four seams is two inches of girth attributed to the pattern.

claims.claim: A fitting is valid only over the undergarments that will be worn with the finished garment, and in shoes of the heel height that will be worn with it.
claims.source_support_note: Kaynaklar ÖLÇÜM koşulu için söyler (S-0002 iç giyim, S-0003 ayakkabı); kitap onu PROVA oturumuna genişletir.
claims.risk_note: Bust position and waist level shift with underwear; the reader diagnoses the underwear and cuts the pattern.

claims.claim: Grain and balance are read first, because a garment hanging off-grain makes every reading below it unreliable. This is a rule about the order of READING and it is this book's own; no source states it as a sequence. The order of CORRECTING is separate and is sourced: work from the shoulder or neck downward.
claims.risk_note: Reading local signs first produces a list of symptoms of one upstream fault.

claims.claim: A fitting that never moves is incomplete: arms overhead, arms forward and folded across the chest, bending, sitting on a hard chair, and a full stride each reveal ease shortfalls that are invisible while standing still.
claims.risk_note: Garment passes the fitting and fails in wear; reader loses trust in the method.

claims.claim: Only one variable may be changed per test. Authoritative pattern-alteration guidance states the rule directly, and the reason is that two simultaneous changes cannot be attributed to either.
claims.source_support_note: S-0003 BİREBİR 'Make only one alteration at a time' der; bu bir DÜZELTME kuralıdır. Kitap onu PROVA TESTİNE genişletir ve genişletme kitabındır.
claims.risk_note: Reader cannot learn which change worked and cannot record a reusable amount.

claims.claim: Cutting the pattern is not reversible, so tests escalate by cost: change the fitting condition, then pin, then add a strip at a slash, then slash the fitting garment. The fitting garment exists to be cut and cutting it is not the thing being avoided — what is avoided is cutting the pattern, and removing fabric from an edge, which cannot be undone even on a toile.
claims.risk_note: Irreversible damage to a pattern on an unconfirmed hypothesis.

claims.claim: A diagnostic cycle is not complete until the change has been applied and the region re-observed. A sign that is reduced but not gone has two possible explanations that must be distinguished: the cause was right and the amount too small, which is the commoner case, or a second cause is present as well.
claims.risk_note: Reader stops at partial improvement with no next step — the failure mode named in adversarial finding B-01.

claims.claim: A fold's own line tells you which dimension the surplus lies in: a vertical fold means surplus width, a horizontal fold means surplus length. The rule applies ONLY after the mark has been classified as a fold rather than a pull — a taut horizontal wrinkle means the opposite, a shortage of circumference at that level.
claims.risk_note: The most-used rule in the book. If the axis is wrong, readers shorten what should be narrowed.

claims.claim: Fabric standing in folds indicates too much ease; fabric being pulled or strained indicates too little. Direction is not part of this test and is established separately, afterwards.
claims.source_support_note: S-0004 BİREBİR: 'Too little ease will produce wrinkles that pull and draw the fabric. Wrinkles that lie in folds indicate too much ease.'
claims.risk_note: Confusing the two reverses the direction of every adjustment.

claims.claim: Drag lines lie along the direction of pull. Where several converge, the convergence point is the candidate site. A single drag line has two ends and cannot on its own say which end carries the fault.
claims.risk_note: If drag lines do not point at their source, step 4 of the cycle (locate) has no mechanism.

claims.claim: A defined list of ordinary non-pattern conditions produces fit signs that are easily mistaken for pattern faults, and the list is walked once at the start of a fitting before any pattern diagnosis is accepted.
claims.risk_note: Every downstream diagnosis is contaminated; the reader alters a correct pattern.

claims.claim: On a correctly cut and correctly hanging garment the lengthwise grain runs perpendicular to the floor and the crosswise grain runs parallel to it.
claims.source_support_note: S-0004 BİREBİR: 'The lengthwise grain should be perpendicular to the floor. The crosswise grain should be parallel to the floor.' — S-0003'ün uyum listesi aynısını söyler.
claims.risk_note: Off-grain cutting mimics almost every asymmetric fit sign in the book.

claims.claim: A pattern printed at home must be verified against its printed test square, measured in both directions because some printers scale differently along and across the paper, before any measurement is taken from it. No standards body publishes a tolerance; the working figure is practitioner convention.
claims.risk_note: A pattern printed at 97 percent is diagnosed as a body that is 3 percent larger.

claims.claim: Two ordering rules are established by the sources this book works from — length before width, working downward from the shoulder or neck; and crotch depth before crotch length. Two more follow from the geometry rather than from any source: a sleeve cannot be fitted into an armhole that is still changing, and a sleeve cap is derived from the finished armhole. A fifth rule — working from the upper body downward — is contested: a competing published method orders by dependency instead, doing first whatever affects other areas of fit.
claims.source_support_note: İki kural BİREBİR kaynaklıdır (S-0003 boy-önce-genişlik; S-0002 derinlik-önce-uzunluk); diğer ikisi kitabın GEOMETRİK türetmesidir ve metin bunu söyler.
claims.risk_note: ÖNCEKİ HÂLİ dördünü de 'established' sayıyordu. Depodaki kaynaklarda İKİSİNİN karşılığı vardır; diğer ikisi bu kitabın GEOMETRİK türetmesidir ve bir kaynak (S-0001) bazı kol düzeltmelerinde bağımlılığı TERS yönde işletir (kol değişince beden yan dikişi düzeltilir). Türetme yine de doğrudur ama 'yerleşik uygulama' DEĞİLDİR ve artık öyle sunulmuyor.

claims.claim: A hem that hangs unevenly is read last, because it is usually a consequence of a length or balance fault above it rather than a fault of its own.
claims.risk_note: Levelling the hem hides the upstream fault and makes it undiagnosable.

claims.claim: An adjustment is only reusable if the amount survives the session in a form that can be applied again. Authoritative practice records it on the pattern itself; recording it additionally as a number is what makes it transferable to a different pattern.
claims.source_support_note: S-0002 BİREBİR: 'If you make any changes, mark them on the pattern so it will be correct the next time you use it.' Sayı olarak da kaydetme kitabın eklemesidir.
claims.risk_note: The fit profile — the book's main deliverable — becomes unusable.

claims.claim: An adjustment that recurs across patterns from more than one pattern company is evidence about the body rather than about any one pattern. Within a single company it is not, because every house drafts from its own block.
claims.risk_note: Book 3's premise. If false, the series bridge is a sales argument rather than a technical one.

claims.claim: A dart points toward the fullest part of the curve it shapes and stops before reaching it. Two published guides state this; neither gives a distance, and this book does not supply one.
claims.source_support_note: S-0004: 'Darts should point toward [but] stop short of the fullest part of the area they shape.' S-0007: 'A dart… should point toward the fullest part of the curve it is intended to fit… Darts usually should end before they reach the fullest part (crown) of the curve.' İKİSİ DE MESAFE VERMEZ; kitabın 'küçük adımlarla yaklaştır' talimatı kendisine aittir. ⚠ S-0007 taranmış bir arşiv belgesidir (1963) ve `verification_level` YÜKSELTİLMEMİŞTİR — o yüzden bu iddianın kanıt düzeyi S-0004'ün tam metnine dayanır.
